task.description: Independent re-verification of ELIXIR-DEV's ISS-0418 per-test wasm_hang subprocess isolation implementation: idiom/scope review, both documented design deviations, the regression fix in the harness test file, and repeated-run evidence, re-run from scratch rather than trusted from the handoff.

result.note:
This is a test-harness Mix task, not OTP/supervision runtime code -- questions 1/2 of the REVIEWER charter (gen_statem idiom, InstanceSupervisor isolation) do not apply to this diff; confirmed by `git diff --stat 1e3a1d6f..HEAD -- lib/letflow/` showing only a new design-doc file added under lib/letflow/design/, and an explicit empty diff on lib/letflow/engine/wasm/invocation_lease.ex -- production wasmex call sites (PluginHandler.run_guest/3, PluginInterface.invoke/2,3) genuinely untouched. Only 3 real code files changed: lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex, test/letflow/engine/wasm/plugin_handler_test.exs, test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_test_test.exs -- matches the handoff's claim exactly.

COMPILE/FORMAT: `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` clean (no output). `mix format --check-formatted` on all 3 changed files: exit 0, clean.

DESIGN FIDELITY (§4): read the actual diff against design §4.1-§4.3. discover_wasm_hang_tests/0 runs `mix test --only wasm_hang --dry-run` via the existing stream_and_capture/2 helper (reused verbatim, not modified). run_single_wasm_hang_test/1 issues `mix test "#{file}:#{line}"` with no --only suffix, exactly per §4.1, with an inline comment explaining why the suffix is deliberately absent (citing the design doc). Aggregation in run_wasm_hang_tests/0 matches §4.3 steps 3-6: partitions results into failing/passing, prints full output of every failing subprocess before Mix.raise naming exactly which {file,line} locations failed, applies the ISS-0069 substring check across the concatenation of all N outputs, and reports a single 'OK -- N/N isolated wasm_hang tests passed' line otherwise. Moduledoc's exit-code contract section was updated to describe the N-subprocess shape. This is faithful to the validated design.

DEVIATION (a) -- extract_test_list_block/1's bounded-window FILTER instead of take_while: VERIFIED AS A REAL, NECESSARY ADAPTATION, not a fragile hack. I ran `mix test --only wasm_hang --dry-run` myself on this repo and captured the real output: ExUnit's own compiler-warning re-emission for unrelated files (e.g. test/support/tenant_slug_test.exs's register_test/4 deprecation warnings) genuinely interleaves BETWEEN the 'Tests that would be executed:' header and the real file:line entries, confirmed directly (grep of the captured output shows warning blocks immediately following the header, before any real test line appears). A strict take_while-until-first-mismatch would stop at the first warning line and discover zero tests on some runs purely due to output-ordering noise -- exactly the false-negative scenario the deviation comment describes. The chosen fix (filter every line in the header-to-terminator window for the exact `^test/\S+\.exs:\d+$` shape, applied to the trimmed line) is robust to interleaving because: (1) it never depends on line position, only content; (2) the regex is fully anchored (^...$, matched against String.trim(line) with no partial-match allowance), so a compiler-warning line -- which always carries trailing text ('warning: ...', a caret/pipe diagram, etc) -- cannot spuriously match the shape even if it happens to start with a `test/...exs:N` substring; (3) the terminator lines ('All tests have been excluded.' / 'Finished in') are only ever printed by ExUnit after the full test list has already been printed, so the window cannot close early and truncate real entries. I independently confirmed the real discovery output for this repo's current 5 tagged tests (call_timeout_test.exs:79, host_api_write_test.exs:461, plugin_handler_test.exs:392/155/495) parses correctly end-to-end via my own repeated live runs (below) -- no evidence of a dropped or duplicated location in 9 consecutive live invocations. I cannot construct a realistic ordering variant where this filter would silently miss a real test line without ALSO being a scenario where take_while would do strictly worse (miss more) -- the filter is strictly more permissive/correct than the design's literal wording while preserving its bounding intent.

DEVIATION (b) -- ignoring the discovery subprocess's exit code: VERIFIED MYSELF, independently, not trusted from the handoff. I ran `mix test --only wasm_hang --dry-run` (real, currently-tagged tests exist) and separately `mix test --only nonexistent_tag_xyz --dry-run` (zero tests match any test in the suite) on this exact repository. BOTH exited 1, with the identical message 'The --only option was given to \"mix test\" but no test was executed' -- confirming the deviation's claim that this exit code carries no information distinguishing 'discovery found N real tests' from 'discovery found zero tests' from 'discovery is broken.' Ignoring it and using the parsed test-list block as the sole signal is therefore the only reliable option available from this specific Mix/dry-run combination, not a shortcut.

SILENT-ZERO-DISCOVERY RISK -- specifically checked, per this review's explicit charge: discover_wasm_hang_tests/0 DOES have a safeguard against this. If extract_test_list_block/1 returns [] (which is exactly what happens for both 'discovery is broken' and 'zero :wasm_hang tests currently exist,' the same category the design's own §4.2 step 5 groups together), the code hard-fails via Mix.raise/1 with an explicit message ('...its \"Tests that would be executed:\" block was empty or absent. This task cannot tell whether that means zero :wasm_hang tests currently exist or the discovery parse itself is broken, so it is treating this as a hard failure rather than silently passing'). This is exactly the correct behavior and directly closes the scenario I was asked to scrutinize hardest: a future refactor that broke the :wasm_hang tag entirely (e.g. renamed the tag, or a compile error before dry-run could even list anything) cannot produce a vacuous 'OK, N/N passed' -- N would be 0, the parsed list would be [], and the task raises instead of proceeding. Verified this branch is reachable and correctly wired by reading the full discover_wasm_hang_tests/0 body (letflow.check.test.ex lines ~429-448) alongside the live exit-code experiment above. No unaddressed silent-failure risk found here.

IRREDUCIBLE-PAIR COMMENT: confirmed present, immediately above `@tag :wasm_hang` at the AC4 test in test/letflow/engine/wasm/plugin_handler_test.exs (currently resolving to line 495 per live discovery output, function body starts a few lines below the comment block -- consistent with the design's own note that file:line numbers drift slightly over time; the comment text itself explicitly cites 'design iss0418-wasm-hang-test-isolation-fix.md §5' and the prior design doc's §6.3.1, and states the pair must not be split into two test blocks). Matches §5's requirement.

HARNESS TEST REGRESSION FIX: read the full diff of test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_test_test.exs. install_wasm_hang_aware_fake_mix/1 is a reasonable, correct, non-weakening fix: it replaces a static args-blind fake mix (which returned a fixed 'Result: 0 passed' with no 'Tests that would be executed:' block, correctly triggering the new hard-fail-on-empty-discovery path and breaking the one test that reaches run_wasm_hang_tests/0) with an args-aware fake that dispatches on argv shape (--dry-run -> a realistic 1-test discovery block + exit 1, matching real Mix's own always-1 exit code I verified above; the discovered fake file:line -> a passing per-test result; anything else -> a generic pass), on both POSIX and Windows fake-executable variants. This does not touch or loosen any of the test's actual assertions (still asserts 'OK -- no test failures, no ISS-0069 warnings' and partition count) -- it only fixes the fixture to match the new two-phase subprocess shape. Ran `mix test test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_test_test.exs` myself: Result: 6 passed, all 6 genuinely pass.

REPEATED-RUN VERIFICATION (independently reproduced, not trusted from the handoff): temporarily added `@compile :export_all` to letflow.check.test.ex (confirmed via `git status`/`git diff` that this is the ONLY temporary change made), invoked Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.Test.run_wasm_hang_tests/0 directly via `mix run <script>` -- the real discovery subprocess plus 5 real per-test subprocesses each time, no mocking. 1 warm-up run: PASS (27703ms). Then 8 consecutive runs: 8/8 PASS (27295-28058ms each), zero wasm_hang-class failures -- corroborating ELIXIR-DEV's reported 15/15 in my own hands, independently. Reverted the temporary export_all edit; `git status --porcelain` confirms the file is back to byte-identical with its committed state (empty diff), and `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` / `mix format --check-formatted` both re-confirmed clean afterward.

SCOPE: no abstractions, behaviours, or generic plumbing introduced ahead of what this fix needs -- the change is a straightforward discover-then-dispatch restructuring of one existing private function plus two small new private helpers, all scoped to this one Mix task file. No scope creep found.

TYPE-SAFETY: not applicable in any load-bearing sense -- this is build/CI-harness code operating on parsed subprocess text, not a state-transition or domain-modeling surface; wasm_hang_location/wasm_hang_test_result are already typed as @type tuples/maps appropriately. No new class of representable-invalid-state issue found worth filing under docs/issues/.

AC CORRECTION STILL OWED: confirmed docs/issues/ISS-0418.yaml exists but does NOT yet contain the design's §1.1 recommended AC correction (no 'AC-NEW' or dated 'SATISFIED...but NOT SUFFICIENT' annotation found by grep). ORCH/DOC-UPDATER still needs to apply this as a separate step before this issue can be considered fully closed -- flagging per the task instructions, not blocking this REVIEWER gate on it since it is explicitly DOC-UPDATER's own step per the design doc and the ELIXIR-DEV handoff already surfaces it.

VERDICT: PASS. No defects found. The two documented deviations are genuine, verified-live, necessary, and correctly scoped adaptations of the design rather than silent hacks; the highest-risk scenario (vacuous zero-test pass) has an explicit, correctly-wired hard-fail safeguard; the pre-existing test regression fix is sound; repeated-run evidence reproduces cleanly in my own hands.
